name: Ajrakh Block Printing
brief: Ancient geometric resist-block printed textile tradition utilizing natural indigo, madder, and pomegranate peel.
key_facts: Traditional 16-step resist and mordant printing process known as 'Tiyar'.
Features double-sided printing (Biti) so both sides appear identical.
Predominant geometric cosmos motifs reflecting Sufi geometric harmony.
Khatri community has practiced this craft for over 400 years along the Indus valley riverbed.

name: Paithani Weaving
brief: Opulent handloom silk saree characterized by pure gold and silver zari pallus with kaleidoscope parrot and peacock motifs.
key_facts: Woven using the tapestry technique where weft threads are interlocked by hand without shuttles.
Classic motifs include Mor (peacock), Popat (parrot), and Asawali (flowering vine).
No loose threads at the back; identical reverse finish distinguishes authentic Paithani.
Patronized by the Satavahana rulers dating back to 200 BC.

name: The India Report (1958)
brief: Foundational treatise on design education and industrial craft that directly recommended establishing the National Institute of Design (NID).
key_facts: Commissioned by the Indian Ministry of Commerce and Industry at the recommendation of Gautam and Gira Sarabhai.
Extensively celebrated the Indian 'Lota' as a benchmark of ergonomics, fluid mechanics, and tactile culture.
Emphasized training students to serve fundamental human needs rather than superficial styling.
Led directly to the establishment of NID in Ahmedabad in 1961.

name: The Amul Mascot
origin: daCunha Agency (Sylvester da Cunha & Eustace Fernandes, 1966)
brief: India's longest-running topical advertising campaign featuring the mischievous hand-drawn girl in a polka-dot frock.
key_facts: Created in 1966 as a competitor response to rival butter brand Polson's mascot.
Art direction and signature hand-drawn style developed by Eustace Fernandes.
Known for rapid topical puns on national current affairs, Bollywood, sports, and politics.
Pioneered the famous tagline: 'Utterly Butterly Delicious'.

name: Palm Leaf & Birch Bark Manuscripts
brief: Indigenous bio-materials that preserved India's monumental epics, astronomical treatises, and medical samhits.
key_facts: Tada-patra (Palm leaf): Sourced from Talipot and Palmyra palms, incised with iron styluses and bound with central cords.
Bhurja-patra (Birch bark): Inner parchment-like bark of Betula utilis, predominant in Kashmir and Central Asian trade routes.
Charcoal, soot lampblack, and sesame oil used to make permanent waterproof indelible inks.
Directly shaped India's horizontal manuscript folio layout (pothi format).

name: Rani ki Vav & Adalaj Stepwells
brief: Masterpieces of subterranean subterranean water harvesting and Solanki architectural engineering.
key_facts: Inverted temple architecture designed to preserve subterranean water tables in arid regions.
Rani ki Vav features over 500 principal sculptures across seven descending terraced levels.
Acts as a natural micro-climate pavilion, maintaining interior temperatures 5-6°C cooler than the surface.
Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site and featured on the reverse of the Indian 100-rupee currency note.
